paper_title: Charge Generation Dynamics in Efficient All-Polymer Solar Cells: Influence of Polymer Packing and Morphology

qa_pairs.question: Compare the power conversion efficiency (PCE) and short-circuit current (Jsc) of all-polymer solar cells based on PTB7-Th:PNDIT-HD and PTB7-Th:PNDIT-DT.
qa_pairs.answer: The PTB7-Th:PNDIT-HD blend achieves a significantly higher PCE of 5.96% with a Jsc of 13.46 mA/cm². In contrast, the PTB7-Th:PNDIT-DT blend yields a lower PCE of 3.25% and a Jsc of 7.81 mA/cm².
qa_pairs.source_title: Charge Generation Dynamics in Efficient All-Polymer Solar Cells: Influence of Polymer Packing and Morphology

qa_pairs.question: How does shortening the alkyl side chain from 2-decyltetradecyl (DT) to 2-hexyldecyl (HD) in the PNDIT acceptor affect its thermal properties?
qa_pairs.answer: Shortening the side chain increases the melting temperature (Tm) from 236.6 °C to 277.9 °C and the crystallization temperature (Tc) from 229.6 °C to 260.0 °C, indicating that shorter side chains promote higher thermal stability and easier crystallization.
qa_pairs.source_title: Charge Generation Dynamics in Efficient All-Polymer Solar Cells: Influence of Polymer Packing and Morphology

qa_pairs.question: In ultrafast transient absorption spectroscopy (TAS) of PTB7-Th blends, what physical processes do the peaks at 0.85 eV, 1.1 eV, and 1.45 eV represent?
qa_pairs.answer: The negative band at 0.85 eV corresponds to the excited state absorption of singlet excitons, the weaker band at 1.1 eV represents polaron absorption, and the positive peak at 1.45 eV is attributed to the stimulated emission (SE) of excitons.
qa_pairs.source_title: Charge Generation Dynamics in Efficient All-Polymer Solar Cells: Influence of Polymer Packing and Morphology

qa_pairs.question: What is the relationship between charge generation efficiency and external quantum efficiency (EQE) in the PTB7-Th:PNDIT-HD and PTB7-Th:PNDIT-DT blends?
qa_pairs.answer: There is a direct correlation between the two; the PTB7-Th:PNDIT-HD blend shows a charge generation efficiency of ~64% and a corresponding EQE of ~65% (at 1.75 eV). Conversely, the PTB7-Th:PNDIT-DT blend shows a lower charge generation efficiency of ~30% and an EQE of ~35%.
qa_pairs.source_title: Charge Generation Dynamics in Efficient All-Polymer Solar Cells: Influence of Polymer Packing and Morphology

qa_pairs.question: How do the photoinduced electron transfer rates in PTB7-Th:PNDIT-HD and PTB7-Th:PNDIT-DT blends compare to the singlet exciton decay in neat PTB7-Th?
qa_pairs.answer: The photoinduced electron transfer is fastest in the PTB7-Th:PNDIT-HD blend with a half-life of 2.5 ps, followed by the PTB7-Th:PNDIT-DT blend at 8 ps. Both are significantly faster than the 17 ps half-life of singlet exciton decay in neat PTB7-Th.
qa_pairs.source_title: Charge Generation Dynamics in Efficient All-Polymer Solar Cells: Influence of Polymer Packing and Morphology

qa_pairs.question: Why is geminate recombination less dominant in the PTB7-Th:PNDIT-HD blend compared to the PTB7-Th:PNDIT-DT blend?
qa_pairs.answer: Geminate recombination is suppressed in the PTB7-Th:PNDIT-HD blend because both the donor (PTB7-Th) and acceptor (PNDIT-HD) have preferential face-on orientations. This creates correlated domains and interfacial alignment that favors efficient charge separation, whereas geminate recombination remains the dominant depopulation process in the DT-based blend.
qa_pairs.source_title: Charge Generation Dynamics in Efficient All-Polymer Solar Cells: Influence of Polymer Packing and Morphology

qa_pairs.question: Based on GIXS measurements, what are the differences in molecular packing and π-π stacking distances between the PTB7-Th:PNDIT-HD and PTB7-Th:PNDIT-DT blends?
qa_pairs.answer: PTB7-Th:PNDIT-HD exhibits a slightly more face-on geometry and a shorter π-π stacking distance of 3.97 Å, whereas the PTB7-Th:PNDIT-DT blend has a slightly larger π-π stacking distance of 3.99 Å.
qa_pairs.source_title: Charge Generation Dynamics in Efficient All-Polymer Solar Cells: Influence of Polymer Packing and Morphology

qa_pairs.question: Identify the solvent, additive, and donor-to-acceptor ratio used to fabricate the PTB7-Th and PNDIT-R all-polymer solar cells.
qa_pairs.answer: The solar cells were fabricated using a 1.3:1 (w/w) acceptor to donor ratio in chloroform, with 1.0 vol % diiodooctane (DIO) as an additive.
qa_pairs.source_title: Charge Generation Dynamics in Efficient All-Polymer Solar Cells: Influence of Polymer Packing and Morphology
